label: Confusion & hard decisions
title: Bhagavad Gita on Hard Decisions: 7 Verses for Clarity
description: Seven verses for a choice you keep circling, from Arjuna's 'I don't know' (2.7) to Krishna's 'reflect fully, then choose' (18.63). Sanskrit, plain English and one thing to try.
h1: Bhagavad Gita on hard decisions: 7 verses for clarity
subtitle: For the choice you keep going round in circles on. Read one a day, or all seven before you decide.
keywords: what to do when confused bhagavad gita
intro: The whole Gita answers one undecided man. Arjuna admits he doesn't know what's right and asks for help. Seventeen chapters later, Krishna hands the choice back to him: reflect on all of it fully, then do as you choose (18.63). These verses follow that arc: admitting confusion, seeing why a divided mind can't move, knowing even the wise get confused, what clear judgement looks like, choosing, and acting with evenness. The last is Arjuna's own answer, from sitting down in 1.47 to standing ready in 18.73.

image.alt: A young man standing still on a footbridge over a highway that splits toward two cities at dusk
image.altGlobal: A young man standing still on a footbridge over a highway that splits toward two cities at dusk

days.heading: Admit you don't know
days.line: I'm confused about what's right. Tell me plainly what's best; I'm ready to learn.
days.forYou: Kārpaṇya-doṣopahata-svabhāvaḥ: Arjuna says his nature is overcome, he's confused about what's right, and he asks plainly to be taught. Clarity in the Gita starts here, with someone honest enough to say 'I don't know'.
days.today: Write the decision as one question. Then write what you're afraid each answer will cost.

days.heading: Why you keep going round
days.line: A decided mind is single and focused. An undecided mind splits into endless branches.
days.forYou: Krishna says the decided mind is single, while the undecided mind branches endlessly. Each option grows its own what-ifs, and those grow more. That's the loop you're in, and it comes from a mind without a single aim yet. Intelligence has nothing to do with it.
days.today: Ask yourself what you most want this decision to protect. Answer in one word.

days.heading: Even the wise get confused
days.line: What is action, and what is inaction? Even the wise are confused about this.
days.forYou: Krishna admits the hard part: even the wise (kavayaḥ) are confused about what to do and what not to do. Struggling with this decision means it's a real choice.
days.today: Talk the decision through with one person who has nothing riding on it.

days.heading: What clear judgement looks like
days.line: Clear judgement knows when to act and when to wait, what to fear, and what frees you.
days.forYou: Krishna describes clear (sāttvika) understanding: it knows when to go forward and when to hold back, what should be done and what shouldn't, what to fear and what not to, what binds and what frees. That's a checklist. Run your choice through it.
days.today: For each option, answer two questions: does this bind me or free me? What am I afraid of, and should I be?

days.heading: Reflect fully. Then choose.
days.line: I've told you all I know. Reflect on it fully, then do as you choose.
days.forYou: Vimṛśyaitad aśeṣeṇa yathecchasi tathā kuru. After seventeen chapters, Krishna hands the choice back to Arjuna: think it through fully, then do as you wish. The choice was always his, and yours is yours.
days.today: Set a deadline for this decision and put it in your calendar.

days.heading: Act, and stay even
days.line: Do the work steadily, letting go of clinging. Stay the same in success and failure; that balance is yoga.
days.forYou: Once you've chosen, Krishna's advice is to act steadily and let go of clinging, staying the same in success and failure. No decision comes with a guarantee, and evenness lets you act anyway.
days.today: Take the first concrete step on your choice today, however small.

days.heading: Arjuna sits down, and stands up

story.title: From 1.47 to 18.73
story.body: At the start of the Gita, Arjuna asks Krishna to drive the chariot between the two armies so he can see who he must fight. He sees teachers, uncles and cousins. His hands shake, his bow slips, and he sits down, refusing to fight (1.47). Eighteen chapters later, after Krishna has told him to reflect fully and choose for himself, Arjuna speaks again: my confusion is gone, my memory has returned; I stand firm, free of doubt, and I will act on your word (18.73).
story.lesson: Arjuna's clarity came from understanding enough to choose.

days.forYou: Arjuna's decision was the hardest anyone in the epic faced. He took his time. He asked, listened, questioned, and then stood up.
days.today: Write what standing up on your decision looks like, in one sentence.
days.line: My confusion is gone, my clarity is back. I stand firm, free of doubt, and I'll act.

faq.q: What does the Bhagavad Gita say about making decisions?
faq.a: The Gita opens with Arjuna unable to decide (1.47, 2.7) and closes with Krishna telling him to reflect fully and then do as he chooses (18.63). Along the way it describes the one-pointed, decided mind (2.41) and clear judgement that knows what to do and what not to do (18.30).

faq.q: What does yathecchasi tathā kuru mean?
faq.a: It ends Bhagavad Gita 18.63: do as you wish. After all his teaching, Krishna leaves the decision to Arjuna, asking only that he reflect on it fully first.

faq.q: Which Gita verse helps when you're confused?
faq.a: 2.7, where Arjuna admits his confusion and asks to be taught, is where clarity starts. 4.16 reminds you that even the wise get confused, and 18.63 tells you to reflect and then choose.
